messages:
alex: Noticed a canary OOM cluster-wide for orca-miniX int4 yesterday during a high-gen campaign. Symptoms: OOMs only when batch_size >= 5 and requested max_new_tokens >= 600.

maria: Saw that spike on the dashboard. host mem usage climbs, then a flurry of small frees and then OOM.

alex: Example micro-log from one host: 
alex: ```
[2026-04-02T14:03:12Z] DEBUG allocator: alloc(256MB) -> ptr=0x7f2a...
[2026-04-02T14:03:12Z] DEBUG allocator: free(ptr=0x7f2a...) -> bucket[64k]+=1
[2026-04-02T14:03:12Z] WARN allocator: freelist_saturation=0.92
[2026-04-02T14:03:13Z] ERROR OOM while alloc 1.1G
```

suresh: Repro confirmed with stress harness. I ran a sweep (batch 1..8, max_new 128..1024) and isolation shows fragmentation threshold hit around batch=5 for this quant layout.

jen: Is this unique to q4_k_mapped or general to our int4 packing?

maria: Only q4_k_mapped so far. int8 and float16 runs fine.

alex: Initial mitigation we discussed: reduce default max_new_tokens for int4 families from 768 -> 300 on canary, and disable aggressive KV prefetch for int4.

suresh: Also prototyped "microbatch stitcher" that breaks a large generation into subrequests of 256 tokens with merge on the server. Works: prevents freelist saturation, but can add ~15-25% latency and complicates token streaming.

jen: Can we make microbatching opt-in per-route or per-customer? We shouldn't surprise latency-sensitive apps.

maria: Yes. Option: default to conservative max_new and offer route-level flag allow_high_max which will enable microbatch+prefetch tuning. We'll surface the tradeoffs in the Console.

alex: I also pushed a small allocator tweak to run the slot-compactor at lower interval for int4 hosts (PR #4781). That reduces small-fragment buildup in long-running instances.

infra-bot: Canary rollout: default max_new_tokens change applied to orca-miniX-int4 canaries (PR 4781 + 4782). Monitoring window 30m.

maria: Smoke after rollout: 30m no OOMs on canary, p95 latency up ~10ms with prefetch off.

suresh: Microbatch patch results: no OOMs even at batch 8 + max_new 1024 in harness. Tail latency stable. Need to validate streaming/stop token behaviour for stitched outputs.

jen: Action list:
- maria: make the canary default change permanent and update onboarding docs (max_new_default=300 for int4) [ETA: EOD]
- suresh: finish microbatch stitch integration tests (streaming + stop tokens) and perf bench [ETA: 72h]
- alex: add freelist_saturation metric and alert when >0.85 for 10m; add auto-fallback policy to int8 for that scenario [ETA: this sprint]
- infra: evaluate slot-compactor interval tradeoffs in prod (PR 4781) [ETA: next week]

alex: Filing a short playbook note summarizing root cause: int4 allocation churn + prefetch + large max_new_tokens -> freelist exhaustion -> OOM. Mitigations: default cap, opt-in microbatching, allocator compactor frequency, runtime fallback to int8.

maria: I'll draft the playbook and include recommended default settings and the console flags.

infra-bot: Created ticket ML-2329 (microbatch integration) and ML-2330 (freelist metric + fallback).

suresh: Also adding a stress job to run daily for orca-miniX-int4 at peak gen shapes so we catch regressions early.

jen: Thanks team. Let's review after suresh's integration tests.
